title: Write and Represent Inequalities
objective: I can write inequalities to represent real-world situations.
model: word phrase to symbol (<, >, ≤, ≥), checked against a number line ray with a closed or open circle

widgets.component: readiness: compare decimals, count whole numbers strictly between 3 and 8, tap the greatest whole number below 7, order decimals
widgets.root: Strict versus inclusive boundaries are exactly what the lesson turns on; keys checked (6 < 6.5, 4, 6, 0.25-0.5-0.75). 1.3 is a real number-line widget.

widgets.component: words to inequality and inequality to words: at least, no more than, more than, fewer than, maximum, no fewer than
widgets.root: Keys verified; wrong choices carry the named slips (strict instead of inclusive, wrong direction, forgot the given amount 230). Challenge 5.3 (at most 9 cars gives 10 values) correctly counts 0.

widgets.component: find the wrong step: at least 16 written > 16, no fewer than 9 written < 9, no more than read as greater than, 7 > n for 'more than 7'
widgets.root: Error step index matches the faulty line in all six; each is a documented misconception for this lesson.

widgets.component: is x = 10 a solution; phrase to symbol; boundary number and 'is it allowed' 1/0
widgets.root: Bins verified (x ≥ 10, x ≤ 15, x > 8 in; x > 10, x < 10, x ≤ 5 out). The 1/0 table keys check (18/1, 40/0, 25/1, 9/0).

widgets.component: generated word-to-inequality, symbol-choice, smallest/largest whole number and 'which phrase means w ≥ 58' items
widgets.root: 8 seeds at each level: every key right (below 49 gives <, a minimum of 9 gives ≥, largest whole number below 74 is 73).

widgets.component: 'Which description tells how to graph the allowed values on a number line?' with choices such as 'Open circle at 61, shaded left'
widgets.root: Choosing the circle type and shading direction is the objective of 8-5 (I can graph the solutions of an inequality). 8-4's canon only READS a given ray (Watch me, Explore) and its vocabulary has no open or closed circle. The item also describes a picture in words rather than showing one.
widgets.replacement: Replace the graph-description template with a read-the-graph item: render a parametric nline viz (ray from the boundary, open flag, direction) and ask 'Which inequality does the graph show?' with the four symbols on the same boundary, as Challenge 2.3 already does. Keep the L3 slot for decimals ('at least 12.5 cups'). Misconception to trap: filled circle read as >, ray direction read as the wrong symbol family.

widgets.component: build the inequality from a story: pick the variable, the symbol and the number
widgets.root: Read assets/studio-act/ineq.js mkWrite: stories with distractor variables, decimals at L3, flagged phrases ('at least', 'no more than'); the student assembles the inequality, so the symbol choice is produced, not recognised.

widgets.component: graph of every weight a crane can lift, choose w ≤ 12
widgets.root: Rendered the viz spec: closed circle at 12, ray left; key w ≤ 12 is right; svg carries width/height/viewBox.

widgets.component: 'Which speed is NOT possible for the getaway car?' with 45, 60, 65, 70 mph
widgets.root: The stem states no speed limit. The 65 mph limit exists only in 5.2 and 5.3, so a student reading 5.1 cold cannot know that 70 is the impossible speed.
widgets.replacement: Put the limit in the stem: 'The getaway car must obey s ≤ 65 mph. Which speed is NOT possible?' and keep the four choices; or attach the number-line viz of s ≤ 65 so the closed circle at 65 shows that 65 is possible.
